source.title: An interactive introduction to grokking and mechanistic interpretability

record.file_problem: The provided text is the full post, but it summarizes and links to a separate interactive article whose full contents are not included.
record.tranche_reason: The post reports qualitative results from training and interpreting networks on algorithmic tasks, but provides no detailed accuracy trajectory or numerical measurements.
record.gate_note: The post reports qualitative findings only. The linked interactive article is not included, so its visualizations and any unreported details cannot be extracted.
record.test_reason: The post reports the author's own qualitative observations from training MLPs on modular addition and sparse parity: weight decay pruning connections during generalization, and larger models using the same Fourier 'star' solution. It gives no numbers, so the evidence is weak and mostly expository.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The author also says the post largely agrees with Quintin Pope's view that grokking is not a big deal. He is surprised the simple 1-layer MLP construction took so long to find, and doubts that crisp mechanistic explanations will scale to complex models.
record.recipe_differences: An interactive exposition and qualitative training/mechanistic analysis, not a detailed reproduction of the original accuracy-trajectory and training-set-size measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The post says grokking depends on hyperparameters being suitable but does not identify which settings.

fits_no_version.finding: AdamW can oscillate between low train loss and low weight norm.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: AdamW with weight decay can show oscillations between fitting the training data and shrinking the weights in grokking setups.

record.code_released: https://github.com/PAIR-code/ai-explorables/tree/master/source/grokking (linked as the source of custom visualizations; training code is not stated)
record.problems: Qualitative summary only; no numerical results, uncertainty estimates, model counts, detailed hyperparameter settings, or accuracy trajectories are provided. The linked interactive article is not included.
record.rows_left_out: No separately reported results beyond those recorded in R1–R5 appear in the provided post text.

untested.parts: The jump from chance to near-perfect test accuracy, the size of the delay, and the dependence on training-set size.
Continuous progress measures that anticipate the jump, and the timing of Fourier circuit formation in modular addition.
Critical dataset size and ungrokking. Weight decay pruning is only described.
Comparisons across architectures and hyperparameters, and the number of runs.
Whether optimizer or numerical controls remove the delay.

missing.what: The training trajectory visualizations and the per-model Fourier analyses in the linked interactive article, which are not in the text provided.
The qualitative statement that the generalizing phase of the modular-addition MLP shows periodic weight patterns.

record.verdict_notes: This is an expository post linking to an interactive article. All the evidence is qualitative, so the labels are weak. The hyperparameter-sensitivity point is credited to Omnigrok rather than shown with new data.

versions.untested_parts: No train/test accuracy values or trajectories are given; the training-set-size effect and delay length are not reported.
The post does not report continuous progress measures anticipating the generalization jump or quantify the timing of circuit formation and removal.
No non-algorithmic datasets or initialization-scale or weight-norm switch tests are reported.
No LLM pretraining or fine-tuning on realistic data is reported.
Weight decay is mentioned pruning spurious connections, but the efficiency account, critical dataset size, and ungrokking prediction are not tested.
The post does not give model counts, architecture or hyperparameter comparisons, or a detailed identification procedure.
An AdamW oscillation is mentioned, but the post does not test whether optimizer or numerical choices produce or eliminate grokking delays.

rows.subject: MLP (modular addition; sizes not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Reports that grokking occurs only under suitable hyperparameters.
rows.measure: Grokking occurrence; no accuracy or delay measure stated.
rows.value: The post says grokking happens only when hyperparameters are just right.
rows.note: This reports a hyperparameter dependency, but does not specify the settings or establish the train/test accuracy pattern or delay.
rows.check: The point is credited to Omnigrok and is only qualitatively re-confirmed ('training lots of models'). There are no settings, accuracies or delay values.

rows.subject: Model trained on sparse parity (architecture and size not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Trains on sparse parity and describes weight decay pruning spurious connections during generalization.
rows.measure: Qualitative change in connections during generalization.
rows.value: Weight decay prunes spurious connections as the model generalizes.
rows.note: The post gives no connection counts or timing.
rows.check: The observation is qualitative only, with no timing or connection counts. It is on sparse parity, not modular addition.

rows.subject: Larger models trained from scratch (model names and count not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Applies a discrete Fourier transform to inspect the models' modular-addition solutions.
rows.measure: Presence of the same star trick in the learned solution.
rows.value: The post reports that larger models use the same star trick.
rows.note: Reported collectively, without model count or per-model results.
rows.check: The row says nothing about gradual formation or later removal of memorization, so it should not link to V2. It bears only on V6. No model count or size is given.

source_check.locator_found: Post, gif/twitter summary, lines 21–23: constructed smaller model and Fourier inspection of larger models trained from scratch.

rows.subject: ReLU model for modular addition (size not stated)
rows.operation_detail: Compares the ReLU construction with an exact solution and describes constructive interference compensating for its error.
rows.measure: Qualitative closeness to the exact solution and constructive interference.
rows.value: The ReLU activation has a small error, but the post says it is close enough for constructive interference to patch everything up.
rows.note: No error magnitude or direct accuracy result is stated.
rows.check: This is about how exact the ReLU construction is compared with an x² activation. It is not about gradual circuit formation or progress measures, so it should not link to V2.

rows.subject: AdamW-trained model (task and size not stated)
rows.measure: Qualitative oscillation between train loss and weight magnitude.
rows.value: The post says AdamW oscillates between low train loss and low weights.
rows.note: This does not report whether the oscillation produces or removes a grokking delay.
